short_definition: A hard credit inquiry is a lender's check after you apply for credit and can slightly lower your score; a soft inquiry is a background check that doesn't affect your score.
explanation: A hard inquiry happens when you apply for credit and a lender checks your file to decide. It is also called a hard pull or hard search. Applications for credit cards, loans, mortgages and sometimes phone contracts trigger one, and you generally have to authorise it. Soft inquiries include checking your own credit, using pre-qualification or eligibility tools, and reviews by lenders you already have accounts with. You can see soft inquiries on your report, but lenders don't use them to judge you.

Several hard inquiries in a short time can signal to lenders that you are seeking a lot of new credit. One inquiry usually has a small, temporary effect. In the US, for example, hard inquiries typically stay on a report for about two years, and their effect on your score usually fades sooner. Some scoring models count several inquiries for the same type of loan, such as a mortgage or car loan, as one if they happen within a short rate-shopping window.

Shopping around for a better rate can save far more money than a small, temporary score dip costs. Applying for many unrelated credit cards in quick succession is different, because those inquiries add up. How inquiries are recorded and scored differs by country and scoring model, so check how it works where you live.
example: Example (illustrative): Sam compares personal loans using three lenders' soft-check eligibility tools, which don't affect his score. He then formally applies only with the lender offering the lowest APR, which triggers one hard inquiry. If he had submitted full applications to all three lenders plus two store cards in the same month, he would have five hard inquiries on file instead of one.
common_mistake: Avoiding checking your own credit report or score out of fear it will hurt it. Checking your own credit is a soft inquiry and does not lower your score.
title: Hard vs Soft Credit Inquiry
